description: Connected speech rules, phonetic reductions, and rhythm differences for Spanish speakers

rules.explanation: Spanish is syllable-timed (every syllable gets roughly equal time). English is stress-timed (stressed words take the rhythm, unstressed words compress).
rules.instruction: Encourage compressing auxiliary words (e.g., 'can you', 'do you', 'would have') into their reduced forms.

rules.condition: Verbs ending in /t/ or /d/ sounds (e.g., wanted, needed, decided)
Verbs ending in voiceless sounds (p, k, f, s, sh, ch) -> worked, stopped, laughed, watched
All other voiced sounds and vowels -> played, lived, called, cleaned

rules.commonMistake: Spanish speakers tend to pronounce -ed as a full separate extra syllable in all verbs ('work-ed', 'play-ed').
